label: Nouns — Food & Drink
description: A 20-question check on food and drink nouns.

questions.prompt: What does «хлеб» mean?
questions.explain: Хлеб means 'bread', as in «Свежий хлеб лежит на столе» (fresh bread is lying on the table).

questions.prompt: What does «молоко» mean?
questions.explain: Молоко means 'milk', as in «Я пью чай с молоком» (I drink tea with milk).

questions.prompt: How would you say 'water' in Russian?
questions.explain: Вода means 'water', as in «Вода в реке очень холодная» (the water in the river is very cold).

questions.prompt: How would you say 'apple' in Russian?
questions.explain: Яблоко means 'apple', as in «Я ем красное яблоко» (I am eating a red apple).

questions.prompt: What grammatical gender is «вода»?
questions.explain: Вода is feminine, shown by the agreeing feminine adjective in «Вода в реке очень холодная».

questions.prompt: What grammatical gender is «вино»?
questions.explain: Вино is neuter, shown by the neuter adjective in «Это вино очень вкусное».

questions.prompt: What grammatical gender is «хлеб»?
questions.explain: Хлеб is masculine, shown by the masculine adjective in «Свежий хлеб лежит на столе».

questions.prompt: What is special about «кофе» grammatically?
options: it is indeclinable (the form never changes)
questions.explain: Кофе is an indeclinable masculine noun, so its form stays «кофе» in every case, as in «Я наслаждаюсь утренним кофе».

questions.prompt: In «В стакане нет воды», what case is «воды» and why?
questions.explain: After «нет» the noun takes the genitive: «воды» marks the absence of water.

questions.prompt: In «Я пью чистую воду каждое утро», what case is «воду»?
questions.explain: «Воду» is the accusative direct object of «пью» (I drink), with «чистую» agreeing in the feminine accusative.

questions.prompt: In «Я мою руки тёплой водой», what case is «водой»?
questions.explain: «Водой» is the instrumental, the means of washing, with «тёплой» agreeing in the feminine instrumental.

questions.prompt: What is the genitive singular of «хлеб» (as in «У нас нет ___ дома»)?
questions.explain: The masculine genitive singular is «хлеба», as in «У нас нет хлеба дома» (we have no bread at home).

questions.prompt: What is the instrumental singular of «молоко» (as in «Я пью чай с ___»)?
questions.explain: The neuter instrumental singular is «молоком», as in «Я пью чай с молоком» (I drink tea with milk).

questions.prompt: What is the prepositional singular of «вино» (as in «В этом ___ мало сахара»)?
questions.explain: The neuter prepositional singular is «вине», as in «В этом вине мало сахара» (this wine has little sugar).

questions.prompt: What is the dative singular of «чай» (as in «Добавь сахар к ___»)?
questions.explain: The dative form is «чаю», as in «Добавь сахар к чаю» (add sugar to the tea).

questions.prompt: What is the genitive plural of «яйцо» (as in «Я купил десять ___»)?
questions.explain: The irregular genitive plural is «яиц», as in «Я купил десять яиц» (I bought ten eggs).

questions.prompt: What is the genitive plural of «гриб» (as in «Дети собрали корзину ___»)?
questions.explain: The masculine genitive plural is «грибов», as in «Дети собрали полную корзину грибов» (the children gathered a full basket of mushrooms).

questions.prompt: What is the nominative plural of «яблоко» (as in «На столе лежат свежие ___»)?
questions.explain: The neuter nominative plural is «яблоки», as in «На столе лежат свежие яблоки» (fresh apples are lying on the table).

questions.prompt: In «Бабушка добавила к супу один гриб», what does the sentence mean?
options: Grandmother took one mushroom out of the soup.
Grandmother added one mushroom to the soup.
Grandmother cooked the soup without mushrooms.
Grandmother bought one mushroom for the soup.
questions.explain: «Добавила к супу один гриб» means she added one mushroom to the soup; «к супу» is the dative goal and «гриб» the accusative object.

questions.prompt: In «Без хлеба обед неполный», what is being said?
options: There is no lunch without water.
questions.explain: «Без хлеба» (genitive after «без») means 'without bread', so the meal feels incomplete; «неполный» means 'incomplete'.
